guard_streams.source: Your right to request a decent broadband service: What you need to know
guard_streams.write_limit: USO thresholds, eligibility and build-cost rules describe a legal request process. They do not prove that a selected parcel currently has service, can order immediately or receives a measured speed.

facts.detail: Ofcom last updated the broadband universal-service guidance on 19 June 2026.
Every UK home and business has the legal right to request a decent affordable connection.
A decent connection is defined as at least 10 Mbit/s download and 1 Mbit/s upload.
Requests are handled by BT, or KCOM in the Hull area.
Applicants do not need to be existing BT or KCOM customers.
BT or KCOM has 30 days to confirm eligibility and estimated build cost.
Eligibility requires no public broadband scheme coverage expected in the next 12 months.
A service above £59.60 per month can still trigger a request right under the stated rules.
Build or upgrade cost up to £3,400 is not charged to the applicant.
Most connections are expected within 12 months, with some taking up to 24 months.

guard_streams.source: Investigation into BT's compliance with its obligations as a broadband universal service provider
guard_streams.write_limit: The closed enforcement case concerns regulatory compliance and excess-cost methodology. It does not establish current broadband availability or measured performance for any selected parcel.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the investigation on 15 October 2020.
The investigation closed on 29 November 2021.
The case examined BT's compliance with broadband universal-service conditions.
The relevant regulatory conditions were imposed on 6 June 2019.
Ofcom had suspended the investigation in July 2021 following BT assurances.
BT changed its approach for cluster connections where associated excess costs do not exceed £5,000 excluding VAT.
Eligible customers can receive connections when they agree to pay their share of relevant excess costs.
Previously BT required customers in a cluster collectively to pay all excess costs.
BT applied the revised approach retrospectively to existing quotes and payments.
Separate regulatory changes allow BT to await total excess-cost agreement for connections above £5,000 excluding VAT.
